clue.text: To the Cockney a lodger is deceitful Dickensian

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang this phrase stands for a lodger, rhyming on the last word
the pickpocket Jack Dawkins in Oliver Twist goes by this nickname

explanation.surface: A Londoner calls his crafty lodger a character out of Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it; here the phrase rhyming with 'lodger' is also the nickname of the young thief in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are names: rhyming slang for a tenant, and the thieving boy who leads Oliver into Fagin's gang.

clue.text: Almost all object. That's parliament for you!

indicators.note: almost means the word 'all' loses its final letter

parts.note: a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Someone sneering that parliament is nearly every object of complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's ... for you!' is a link; the Althing is Iceland's parliament, one of the oldest in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The Icelandic national assembly is the classic crossword example of a legislature.

clue.text: After today a child will keep near

indicators.note: will keep means the word for a child holds the word for near inside it

parts.note: a tot is a small child
nigh is an old word for near

explanation.surface: A parent promising to keep a child close by tomorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: NIGH goes inside TOT.
explanation.definitionFit: This evening is the part of the day following daytime.

clue.text: Not reliable — i.e. can turn nasty

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters of 'i.e. can turn' are badly mixed up

explanation.surface: Warning that something can suddenly go bad, so cannot be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'nasty' does the shuffling of IECANTURN.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubtful or unpredictable things cannot be depended upon.

clue.text: Charges involving quiet cheats

indicators.note: involving means the word for charges wraps round the letter for quiet

parts.note: dues are fees or charges paid
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Fees that quietly swindle people.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheat someone is to fool or con them, a verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Do nothing jolly with an employee seen entering

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Doing nothing jolly while a worker comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective, but it is old naval slang for a Royal Marine; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel porter stationed at the entrance is the staff member visitors see on arrival.

clue.text: A man withdrawn before receiving discharge

indicators.note: receiving means the word for before takes the other word inside it

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
to emit is to discharge

explanation.surface: A man retreats ahead of being given his discharge from the army.
explanation.walkthrough: EMIT goes inside ERE, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious recluse is a man who has retreated from society, a hermit.

clue.text: A fast start

parts.note: fast is read as a period of abstaining from food, not speed: the day on which Lent begins

explanation.surface: A quick getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' wants to mean quick; it is the Lenten fast, which begins on this day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian season of Lent, a forty-day fast, opens on this day.

clue.text: It's diabolical encompassing a strike so

indicators.note: encompassing means the word for 'so' goes around the other pieces

parts.note: sic is Latin for 'so, thus', used to flag a quotation as printed
to tan someone is to beat or strike them

explanation.surface: Someone condemns a walkout as fiendishly wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' looks like industrial action but means to hit, TAN as in tanning someone's hide; A TAN goes inside SIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something devilish or fiendish is said to be of the Devil, Satan.

clue.text: Changeable — change one part

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A note on adjustable machinery: alter just one component.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ONE PART are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: After the sea god Proteus, who could take any shape, the word describes something that keeps changing form.

clue.text: A doctor sees things scattered around — women's wear

indicators.note: scattered around means the letters of the pieces before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor sees clothes strewn about a woman's room.
explanation.walkthrough: DR plus SEES THINGS is rearranged; the clue's 'secs' is a misreading of 'sees'.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose gowns worn to bed are garments for women.

clue.text: Means of expression used by washerwoman

definitions.text: Means of expression used by washerwoman

parts.words: Means of expression used by washerwoman
parts.note: expression is read literally as pressing out, the device a laundress turns to squeeze water from clothes, not a way of speaking

explanation.surface: A laundress's turn of phrase or idiom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expression' suggests speech, but it means squeezing out: the old mangle-like device pressed water out of wet washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangle with rollers squeezes, or presses out, the water from laundry.

clue.text: Two thousand and one going inside celebrated, being calculating

indicators.note: going inside means the pieces for the numbers are placed within the word for celebrated

parts.note: to celebrate someone in song is to have sung their praises
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone toasting the new millennium, 2001, with calculated motives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two thousand and one' reads like the year but gives Roman numerals MM and I; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding up figures is a form of computing or reckoning.

clue.text: A number work in the garden

definitions.meaning: any of the figures 0 to 9 is called this
read as two words, an instruction to turn over the soil with a spade

explanation.surface: Gardening task number one: get digging.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as DIG IT, the second sense is an order to spade over a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A single numeral is a figure; turning soil with a spade is the gardening sense.

clue.text: After a party. Navy men start tidying the decking

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
RN is the abbreviation for the Royal Navy

indicators.note: start means only the first letter of 'tidying' is used

explanation.surface: After the party, sailors begin clearing up the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decking' looks like the planks of a ship, but it means decorating; 'After' and 'the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something is to decorate it, so decking is ornamentation.

clue.text: Knock flat a wicket after six balls — put on a hard hat!

indicators.note: after puts the wicket's letter following the six balls

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls bowled
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a wicket
a helm is an old word for a helmet

explanation.surface: A batsman is out after an over and is told to put his helmet on.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six deliveries in cricket; 'put on' adds HELM.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush or overpower is to flatten completely.

clue.text: -That's Life" broadcast — exit scene-shifters!

indicators.note: shifters suggests the letters of the two words before it are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A broadcast of the TV show That's Life ends with stagehands leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of EXIT SCENE are rearranged; That's Life was a BBC consumer TV programme, and 'That's' and 'broadcast' only dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alive, simply being, is the state of living.

clue.text: Cutting equipment put right after coin is bent

indicators.note: after puts the letter for right behind the rearranged letters
bent means the letters of 'coin is' are twisted into another order

explanation.surface: A bent coin needs putting right after it has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: COINIS rearranged gives INCISO, then R; 'put' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A front tooth for biting is part of the mouth's cutting kit.

clue.text: One in three allowed on an excursion

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the word for allowed sits beneath the excursion

parts.note: a trip is an excursion
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Only one in three permitted to go on the outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of three babies born together is one of three siblings.

clue.text: A motorist's cautious signal

parts.note: the traffic-light colour shown between red and green, telling drivers to take care

explanation.surface: A driver signals caution.
explanation.walkthrough: At British traffic lights the middle, yellowish light warns drivers to prepare to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow-orange traffic light is named for the fossil resin's colour.

clue.text: It measures the current encountered in a foreign sea

indicators.note: in means the word for encountered goes inside the word for sea

parts.note: mer is French for sea
met is the past tense of meet, encountered

explanation.surface: A device for gauging an ocean current met abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' suggests the sea, but it is electric current, measured in amps.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument gauging amperes measures electrical flow.

clue.text: Poor rise in growth pushing prices up

indicators.note: in means the reversed word goes inside the word for growth

parts.note: a bush is a growth of shrubbery

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means the word for poor is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ill means poor, as in ill health

explanation.surface: A weak rise in growth is driving prices up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' reverses ILL to LLI, placed inside BUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull market is one where traders expect and drive rising share values.

clue.text: Speaking in a row about the firm holding it back

indicators.note: about means the word for a row goes around the rest

parts.note: a din is a noisy row

indicators.note: holding means the abbreviation for firm takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word 'it' backwards

explanation.surface: Office argument over the company's accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IT into TI, which goes inside CO; that sits inside DIN. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One's manner of enunciating words when talking is one's elocution.

clue.text: Poles, both holding a single ecclesiastical office

indicators.note: holding means the two pole letters surround the word for a single

parts.note: N and S stand for the north and south poles
one means a single

explanation.surface: Polish clergy, two of them, sharing one church post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests Polish people, but it is the compass poles N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: In church services the day's set prayers include the ninth hour, an office of the breviary.

clue.text: Capital investment for women in seclusion

definitions.text: Capital investment for women in seclusion

parts.words: Capital investment for women in seclusion
parts.note: capital is read as the head and investment as clothing: headwear for cloistered nuns, not money put into a business

explanation.surface: A financial scheme for women living as recluses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital investment' sounds like finance; it is head (caput) covering, worn by nuns.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth headdresses framing a nun's face are worn by women in convents.

clue.text: Supplementary note the Italian enclosed in possibly distant letter

indicators.note: enclosed in says the note and the article sit inside the word for possibly distant

parts.note: yon means that one over there, which may be far off
PS, postscript, is a note added at the end of a letter
il is the Italian for 'the'

explanation.surface: A postscript in Italian tucked into a letter sent from far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' looks like correspondence, as do 'note' and 'enclosed', but it is an alphabet letter, the Greek U.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek alphabet's twentieth character is named this.

clue.text: Get around some children twin eleven-year-olds

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A request to get around some children, twins aged eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist around or encircle something is to wind about it.

clue.text: Keeping in step with the grievance procedure

definitions.text: Keeping in step with the grievance procedure

parts.words: Keeping in step with the grievance procedure
parts.note: read literally, people walking in step together to air a complaint publicly, rather than following an official workplace complaints process

explanation.surface: Staying in line with official complaints procedures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grievance procedure' suggests an HR process; the cd pictures demonstrators walking together.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonstrators walking through streets to voice objection are on a demo.
